newsitem.title: USA: Calif. water officials hail Clinton budget.
newsitem.headline: Calif. water officials hail Clinton budget.

text.p: California water officials on Thursday hailed President Bill Clinton's commitment of $143 million in new federal funding for the San Francisco Bay-Delta estuary in his 1998 fiscal budget.

"President Clinton's commitment recognizes the critical role the federal government has in restoring the Bay-Delta ecosystem to self-sustaining health for the betterment not only of California's environment but also its economy," Stephen Hall, executive director of the Association of California Water Agencies, said in a statement.

The association said the president followed through in full on the first share of a three-year commitment he and the Congress made last fall when they supported a bill to provide $430 million in federal matching funds for ecosystem restoration in the Bay-Delta.

The bill authorized the expenditures only if California voters passed Proposition 204, a $995 million bond measure for ecosystem restoration and water reliability programs on last November's ballot. The measure, titled the Clean, Safe, Reliable Water Supply Act, passed by a 63 percent margin.

"California voters understood the importance of the Bay-Delta to the state, and now we welcome this support at the federal level," said California state Senator Jim Costa, the author of Proposition 204. "This federal funding will be very helpful to addressing California's long-term water needs."

In addition to providing drinking water to two-thirds of all Californians, the Bay-Delta system provides irrigation water for farms that grow 45 percent of the nation's fruits and vegetables and supports 120 fish species.
